connections.why: Modelling a problem as an abstraction is the first step to choosing an algorithm
Knowing several algorithms lets you reason about which is more efficient
Algorithms are turned into working solutions by writing them as programs
Abstractions are made concrete by choosing how to structure their data
Procedures and functions operate on the data structures a program defines
Languages provide the procedures and functions used to build modular programs
Boolean conditions drive the selection and loops in programs
All data types are ultimately encoded using the same binary digits
Boolean logic underlies the circuits inside computer hardware
Both data and instructions are stored as binary inside the machine
Components must be understood before seeing how they exchange data
Instructions are executed by the hardware and software working together
Programming skills are applied within larger creative projects
Many projects involve collecting and analysing data for known users
Analysed data is shaped into artefacts for a given audience
Projects produce artefacts that are reused, revised and repurposed
Publishing artefacts raises questions of protecting your own identity online
Using technology securely includes safeguarding your identity and privacy
Responsible use means recognising harm and knowing how to report it
